question: is the 4-D polar-Fourier frame a control (a closed-form edit built from it moves the predictor's forecast to the steered twin's) or only a description; and does it extrapolate beyond a half-ring fit?
fitpack_arm: not computed: session2_direction_natural_norm has no FITPACK arm; none added

definitions.err_to_target: circular error (deg) of the predictor-native direction probe (session-2, 480 probe clips, stored alpha) on the step-mean pooled forecast, mean over the carrier's targets
definitions.R: <P_edit - P_src, u(t*) - u(src)> / ||u(t*) - u(src)||^2 in probe output space
definitions.forced_choice_frac: fraction of (carrier, target) pairs whose edited forecast is closer in L2 over the pooled forecast (token mean per predicted step; 4 x 1024 concatenated) to the rendered steered twin's native forecast than to the carrier's unedited native forecast (both session-2 cache); per-carrier fraction, bootstrap over carriers
definitions.recovery_full: probe-free <F_edit - F_src, F_twin - F_src> / ||F_twin - F_src||^2 over the same pooled forecast (1 = all the way to the twin's forecast in projection); forced choice is exactly recovery_full > 0.5, so the fraction is a thresholded version of this graded number
definitions.twin_id_acc: target-specific probe-free readout: fraction of (carrier, target) pairs whose edited forecast change (F_edit - F_src, same pooled forecast) has its highest cosine with that target's twin change (F_twin_j - F_src) among the carrier's 4 twins; chance 0.25; a target-independent edit scores 0.25
definitions.CI: boot_ci: 1000 bootstrap resamples of carriers (clips), seed 0, percentile 95%

sites.P22: pooled: delta on every context token at point 22
sites.D12: object tokens only at point 12 (obj = disk(src)|disk(twin) + 1-patch ring, tubelets 0-3)

conds.own: P22: the delta as built; D12: the delta added to each obj token
conds.natural: P22: rescaled to ||twin_meanpool_22 - src_meanpool_22||; D12: unit(delta) x the twin's per-token change at point 12 on each obj token

definitions.task2_units: carriers whose source lies in a fold's span; per carrier, mean over its (fold, target) entries
